lead.headline: U.S. strikes Iranian targets on Qeshm Island on the eve of Election Day
lead.dek: Officials call the Hormuz strikes defensive; Tehran's parliament speaker warns of 'a new battlefield'
body: The U.S. military struck Iranian targets on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz late Monday, three U.S. officials told CBS News, hours before polls opened in the midterm elections. A senior official said the limited strikes answered Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fire at an American aircraft over the strait.

A U.S. official told The Associated Press the strikes hit "Iranians using surface to air missiles against U.S. assets." Iran's state news agency IRNA reported explosions in rapid succession on Qeshm, with witnesses seeing two planes over the island, and Fars reported blasts at Bandar Lengeh. Brent crude, which fell 7.6% to $104.77 Monday on hopes of a deal, rose $1.84 to $106.61 by 7:44 GMT, Al Jazeera reported.

Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Tuesday that any U.S. "strategic error" would open "a new battlefield in the war" and that Iran is at its highest defensive readiness. Vice President JD Vance said Monday, before the strikes, that he and Trump "feel pretty good" about a negotiated settlement; AP reported Qatari mediators plan more talks this week.

briefs.headline: Voters decide all 435 House seats and a 53-47 Senate as polls open
briefs.summary: More than 54 million ballots were cast before Election Day, nearly half the 2022 midterm total, NPR reported. Democrats need a net gain of three House seats and four in the Senate; 36 governorships are also on the ballot.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court refuses to make California set aside 20,000 ballots
briefs.summary: The one-line unsigned order, with no noted dissents, denied DOJ's bid to segregate mail ballots from alleged noncitizens; more than 6 million California mail ballots are already in.

briefs.headline: Judge tosses DOJ case against two ex-FBI officials
briefs.summary: Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui threw out charges that Bradley Benavides and Nikki Floris lied to Congress in 2023, calling the prosecution "weaponization." DOJ said it is weighing options.

briefs.headline: NTSB sees signs Learjet broke up before Palm Beach crash
briefs.summary: Board member Tom Chapman said there is evidence of "some breakup" before impact; the jet reported an over-speed descent at 12:48 p.m. Families named the seven passengers, two of them children.

briefs.headline: Russian bombs kill 29 at Zaporizhzhia aid hub, Ukraine says
briefs.summary: Acting governor Mykhailo Semikin said 29 died and 48 are missing at a Komyshuvakha school used to hand out aid. U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff then set Abu Dhabi talks for Nov. 10-11.

briefs.headline: U.S. to drop South Africa and Rwanda from AGOA in January
briefs.summary: Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said both governments' practices are inconsistent with the program's eligibility rules. South Africa shipped $1.7B under AGOA in 2025.

briefs.headline: North Korea denies Binance theft and test-fires cruise missiles
briefs.summary: Kim Yo-jong called the FBI finding that Pyongyang's TraderTraitor group stole $6B a "grave political provocation." The strategic cruise missile launch followed her statement.

briefs.headline: UK doubles wait for permanent residency to 10 years
briefs.summary: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said most foreign workers will wait 10 years, care workers earning 25,000 pounds keep five, and small-boat arrivals could wait 30.

briefs.headline: Wood County jury convicts Casto in 2014 killing of Cindy Ball
briefs.summary: Jurors returned the verdict Monday and recommended no mercy, so Greg Casto, 57, faces life without parole; sentencing is Jan. 15 before Judge J.D. Beane.

briefs.headline: Polls open at 6:30 a.m. after 169,350 early and absentee ballots
briefs.summary: Early and absentee voting Oct. 21-31 ran 15% above the 2022 midterm, about 14% of registered voters, the Secretary of State's office said; polls close at 7:30 p.m.

briefs.headline: Marshall lands $3M federal grant for aerospace manufacturing
briefs.summary: The Economic Development Administration award to Marshall and its ARMOR coalition funds aviation training and defense supply-chain work expected to support nearly 600 jobs.

briefs.headline: UMWA and 52 miners ask justices to force state silica dust rule
briefs.summary: The Oct. 29 petition asks the Supreme Court to make the Board of Coal Mine Health and Safety set limits after federal regulators delayed a 2024 rule; the court said it is likely heard next year.

regional.item: City garbage trucks will reach Enslow Park by Galleries East Road and Ritter Boulevard from Wednesday under the bridge's nine-ton limit.
A bicyclist died after a vehicle hit him on MacCorkle Avenue Southwest in South Charleston Monday evening; the driver stayed, police said.
Wood County's school board hired a consulting team Monday at up to $200 an hour to run finances after its finance director resigned.

away.item: Bennington voters decide a 1% local option tax today, about $1.8 million a year, 69% of it earmarked for property tax relief in year one.

hotspots.item: A Webster Springs man, 20, is charged with attempted arson after allegedly dousing the area around a home with gasoline Oct. 26, The Webster Echo reported Sunday.
Surf City's council votes tonight at 6 on moving its monthly work session to 3 p.m. on the third Thursday, a change settled at its Oct. 15 session.

briefs.headline: Frizzell, new Prince George council take their oaths
briefs.summary: Mayor Garth Frizzell and eight councillors, five of them new, were sworn in Monday night. Frizzell said his plan for the term is due within two weeks.

briefs.headline: Man gets eight years for firing at police near Prince George
briefs.summary: Tyler Suel pleaded guilty Oct. 27 to firing at officers near East Perry Road in May 2025. He also got a 10-year firearms ban; no officers were hurt.

briefs.headline: B.C. First Nations sue to quash Pacific Link designation
briefs.summary: The St'at'imc Chiefs Council and at least seven other nations filed judicial reviews saying Ottawa breached its duty to consult on the 1 million-barrel-a-day line.

briefs.headline: Blackstone, pension funds buy LNG Canada stake for $3.1B US
briefs.summary: The group, including CPP Investments, takes 49.9% of the Mitsubishi unit holding 15% of the Kitimat plant. Phase 2 will double capacity to 28 million tonnes a year.

briefs.headline: Champagne says budget will simplify taxes for small business
briefs.summary: The finance minister told the Canadian Club in Toronto the Nov. 5 budget will also detail the Canada Strong Fund and airport ownership changes.

briefs.headline: CU Boulder projects US fire losses nearly tripling by 2060
briefs.summary: A University of Colorado Boulder CIRES team projected up to 449,100 buildings damaged or destroyed by 2060 without new fire adaptation. The study is in Nature Communications.

briefs.headline: Nagoya method reads single vesicles to locate inflammation
briefs.summary: Nagoya University researchers tagged microRNA inside intact extracellular vesicles and found a kidney-protein pairing enriched in urine from transplant rejection patients, in Cell Reports Physical Science.

briefs.headline: Nature study finds reappraisal measures do not agree
briefs.summary: An international team pooled 40 fMRI data sets and found questionnaire, task and amygdala measures of cognitive reappraisal barely correlated. Detecting the amygdala effect alone would take 1,105 subjects, they wrote.

briefs.headline: Yakima County reports first US H5N1 death of 2026
briefs.summary: Washington's Yakima Health District said a person with underlying conditions and contact with infected dairy cows died after hospitalization; a third case was mild. It is the third U.S. H5N1 death since 2024.

briefs.headline: New York Times sues Brave over scraping for AI companies
briefs.summary: The suit, filed Monday in Manhattan federal court, says the browser maker built a 30 billion-page index and sold publishers' content to Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI and Cohere. Three other papers filed a similar suit.

briefs.headline: Musk throttles Grok Bot, says serving cost outran revenue
briefs.summary: Users found weekly usage limits maxed out over the weekend; SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said on X the cost of serving the agent was "unsustainably high relative to revenue." SpaceX's filing put AI at 52% of company income.

briefs.headline: Goldman Sachs pulls AI coding tools from traders and bankers
briefs.summary: Bloomberg reported, citing internal October guidelines, that only engineers keep access to tools such as Claude Code and GitHub. A Goldman spokesperson cited productivity and risk management.

kicker: Nicholas-Webster and Summers-New River carry no regional line today; the Kyushu basho (tournament) opens Nov. 8 in Fukuoka, five days out.
